To share records between the ERP and the system, you will need to identify 
 several system settings, some of which are defined for a specific functional 
 area (such as shipping or receiving).

This value indicates 
 if the system will include a record for items that have zero (0) quantity 
 currently in the warehouse.The setting does not use the item balance interface upload criteria to filter That is uploaded. The system will include all zero (0) quantity records regardless the item balance interface upload criteria.

Allow 
 Duplicate Receipt IDs On Add?: This value indicates if the system will allow the same receipt ID to exist 
 multiple times in the system. If you select 'Y', the system will allow 
 the interface to download receipt ID's that already exist in the database. 
 If you select 'N', the system checks to see if this receipt ID already 
 exists in the database. If it does, the system will reject the receipt 
 and display an error message saying that the ID already exists and system 
 will not allow duplicates.

Status 
 That New Receipt Records Are Placed In: This value identifies the 
 status that the system will assign to interfaced receipts/lines/containers.

Receiving 
 Upload Level: This value indicates what level (container, detail, 
 or header) is checked for status during an upload.

- Container: Produces data (receipt 
 container level) as soon as the container reaches the upload status, and 
 the container is closed.

- Detail: Produces data 
 (receipt container/detail level) when all other containers on the same 
 receipt line have reached the upload status, and the detail is closed.

- Header: Produces data (receipt container/detail/header level) when all 
 other containers on all receipt lines have reached the upload status, 
 and the header is closed.

Upload 
 Receipt Containers At This Status Or Higher: This value identifies 
 what status a receipt must meet before the system can include its 
 receipt in an upload file. This file provides information about 
 the status of interfaced receipts in the system.

Allow 
 duplicate Shipment IDs On Add?: This value indicates if the system 
 will allow the same shipment ID to exist multiple times in the system.

If you select 'Y', the system will allow the interface to download shipment 
 ID's that have the same shipment ID/warehouse/company.

If you select 'N', the system 
 checks to see if this shipment ID/warehouse/company already exists in the database. If it 
 does, the system will reject the shipment and display an error message 
 saying that the ID already exists and system will not allow duplicates.

Shipping 
 Interface Download Record Types To Create: This value determines 
 what records the system will create when it downloads orders from the 
 ERP. The system can generate shipments, or orders and shipments. Shipments 
 are required to process records in the system.

- Trading Partner Management 
 displays records based on order number, so if you are using this module, 
 select the Orders and Shipments option.
- When this setting is configured for Orders and Shipments, the system copies the Shipment ID to the ERP Order Number field if this field is blank on the order's interface file.

Status 
 That New Shipping Records Are Placed In: This value identifies 
 the status that the system will assign to interfaced shipments, 
 lines, and containers.

Upload 
 Deleted Shipments?: This value allows the upload of deleted shipments 
 when performing a Shipping Upload. These shipments could have been deleted 
 from allocation rejection or short picking when using the "Delete 
 Rejected" Outbound Status Action; or, via manual deletion. Note that 
 the system places the shipment's header and detail information in the 
 UPLOAD_ORDER_HEADER 
 and UPLOAD_ORDER_DETAIL tables until the upload is processed, and the system will mark the record as deleted in the database.

Also, when shipments / shipment lines are configured to include in the upload, the system will use the interface upload criteria records to filter the records when they are written to the upload order tables.

Allow Zero in UD7, UD8, UD9, and UD10 On Download?: This value indicates if you want the system to change the value for User Defined Fields 7-10 to a zero value when it is sent as part of a download interface save or change. If this setting is not activated, then the system will consider an interfaced zero value as no change to these user defined fields, and they will keep their original values. Note that User Defined Fields 9 and 10 are only available on the shipment download.

Delimiter Token: This value 
 indicates which character you want to use to separate fields on a Delimited/Fixed 
 Length text file. Common delimiter tokens include such characters as: 
 +, |, #.

This delimiter token must be a 
 one character value. The token cannot be a letter, number or any symbol 
 that you might include as data. For example, if some addresses use # sign 
 for apartments, do not select this symbol as the delimiter token. The 
 system cannot discern between data and token signs and will not parse 
 the data correctly.

You can use ASCII values to specify a character that cannot be accessed 
 by the keyboard. This is an additional safeguard to ensure that a value 
 is not used as both the token and a value. For example, you could enter 
 the ASCII value 124 to represent | (the pipe bar).

NOTE: Windows considers an asterisk a "wildcard" character 
 (used for general searches), so the system will not allow you enter an 
 asterisk into the System Value Field.

Delimited, 
 Fixed Length, & Direct Modes Only

For interfaced date values that also require a time, the system always assumes the syntax is

. Note that if your date value does not require a time, then the system will tack onto the end a time value of 000000 when saving to the database. This is done because the database requires all date values to have a time appended to them.

                    For interfaced date values that also require a time, the system always assumes the syntax is HHMMSS. Note that if your date value does not require a time, then the system will tack onto the end a time value of 000000 when saving to the database. This is done because the database requires all date values to have a time appended to them.
